name: Nam Du / Hòn Sơn
headline: Rainy island days by the sea.
subheadline: A small photo note from the road.
introduction: An island-sun plan that turned into a rainy Kiên Giang story: Rạch Giá food, sea coffee, lost AirPods, and stormy little lessons.
shortDescription: An island-sun plan that turned into a rainy Kiên Giang story: Rạch Giá food, sea coffee, lost AirPods, and stormy little lessons.
description: An island-sun plan that turned into a rainy Kiên Giang story: Rạch Giá food, sea coffee, lost AirPods, and stormy little lessons.
longDescription: A compact gallery from Kiên Giang.
overview:
I went to Kiên Giang expecting island sun, forest runs, Ma Thiên Lãnh peak, Nam Du, and snorkeling at Hòn Hai Bờ Đập. Instead, five out of seven days came with rain. Not exactly the postcard version, but still a funny little lesson: sometimes the island trip becomes a storm trip.

Rạch Giá food was easy to love, especially grilled dried squid and coffee by the sea. I also lost my AirPods, chased the location for two days, then lost a power bank the day after. That was how the trip signed off.
travelTips: Keep backup plans for rainy days.
Save time for Rạch Giá food and sea coffee.

images.title: Green Outpost in the Shallows
images.story: A string of marker floats trailed away from a tiny, tree-topped islet into the pale green shallows. The overcast sky kept the water cool and flat, with no postcard sunshine in sight. It looked like the kind of place where someone retreated specifically to never answer an email again.

images.title: Trail Marker Over the Bay
images.story: From the hillside path, the cove opened up through wet leaves, dotted with wooden fishing boats riding out the swell. Hand-painted signs nailed to the trunk pointed toward trails that were rapidly turning to slick mud under the grey sky. I paused here to catch my breath and check if my rain jacket was actually waterproof.

images.title: Red Roof in the Canopy
images.story: A single red-tiled roof poked out from the sea of dense jungle halfway up the mountain flank. Down below, wind ruffled the tops of the coconut palms, rustling with every sudden gust rolling off the peak. It sat so high and quiet against the green slope that hiking up felt like a negotiation with gravity.

images.title: Barefoot on the Turquoise Boat
images.story: A fisherman leaned against his weathered turquoise cabin, flashing an effortless smile while our boats drifted alongside each other in the harbor. He stood barefoot on the damp deck, unfazed by the rolling wake and tangled rigging. While I was fretting over damp camera lenses, he looked like he was having the best morning of his week.

images.title: Churning Green Sea Foam
images.story: Leaning over the stern railing, I watched the ferry churn the deep green sea into ribbons of white foam. The rhythmic thrum of the diesel engine drowned out everything else, accompanied by a cool spray hitting my face. Somewhere in these waters, or perhaps back on the pier, my AirPods were living their own separate adventure.

images.title: Coconut Palms Along Rocky Shore
images.story: A row of skinny coconut palms rose along the rocky shoreline, standing dark against the tangled jungle canopy behind them. Huge billows of grey-bellied clouds were stacking up along the ridge, promising another afternoon downpour. We drifted past just long enough to admire the stillness before the first heavy drops hit the surface.

images.title: Grey Sea Beyond Coconut Palms
images.story: Looking down through the wild coconut groves, the entire hillside rolled quietly into a pale, milky sea. Thick cloud cover flattened the horizon, turning the distant fishing boats into tiny dark flecks against the water. Even without the sunny postcard blue, the damp breeze and total silence up here felt like a fair trade.

images.title: Tin Roofs in the Cove
images.story: From the hillside road, the fishing village sat clustered tightly against the bay under a heavy afternoon sky. A handful of boats drifted near the wooden piers, looking steady despite the looming rain that had followed us all week. It was peaceful watching the metal roofs curve around the shore, a quiet close to a trip where the weather had other plans.
